links.outcome: Misattribution or clinical use of incidental small-talk asides in AI-generated notes
links.effect: Frontier models inserted small-talk into 35% of notes; in 3.7% of frontier notes they misattributed the asides or used them clinically; mean quality scores changed by at most 0.20 points.
links.quote: In 3.7% of frontier notes, models misattributed the asides or used them clinically.

links.outcome: Note contamination from background speech from a separate patient encounter
links.effect: Background speech at -10 dB leaked into 48.2% of transcripts, with contamination in 5.3% of downstream notes from four open-weight models (57 mock consultations).
links.quote: In 57 mock recorded consultations, background speech from a separate patient encounter at -10 dB leaked into 48.2% of transcripts, with contamination detected in 5.3% of downstream notes generated by four open-weight models.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLM resistance to incidental information before clinical use
Safeguards preventing contamination from incidental information while preserving clinical reasoning

screen.reason: Evaluates safety vulnerabilities/failure modes of LLMs in ambient clinical documentation and reasoning (specifically small-talk and background speech leakage/contamination) in simulated/mock dialogues without testing a specific deployment guardrail intervention.
